title: Field Report: Statements at the Fire Line, 11:20

fields.organization: Larkspur Constructors, Inc. — Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2
fields.location: West gate muster and Ninth Street Command tape line, Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street; trailer 2 clipboard
fields.inspector: K. Brandt, Field Engineer (west gate recorder)
fields.weather: Overcast, 53°F, wind WSW about 8 mph, ground saturated (0.6 in overnight rain)
fields.summary: At 11:20 the Harlan & Weir print shop manager came to the tape line and spoke to the Engineer of Record (by phone), the competent person and the Safety Director. His words: "Look, that crack on our south wall has been there since 2019. Your gauge is just measuring an old crack. Tell the fire chief my people can go back in and finish the 1 p.m. job." At about 11:21 a pipe crew laborer caught the competent person at the muster. His words: "It wasn't the gas line, it was the rain. That wall was weeping all morning, you even wrote it down. You should've said it was soft at 06:45. Just add a line to the form that you told us to watch it, and nobody gets blamed." Form LC-F-22 for this trench is on the clipboard in trailer 2. It was signed at 06:45 and has one note: 'seepage, south wall, 16+00.' Nothing has been written on it since. This recorder has made no finding on cause.

findings.item: CG-3, Harlan & Weir south foundation (last reading on trailer 2 display)
Print shop south wall, existing crack
findings.notes: The crack is mapped in the pre-construction survey. The wall is 18 ft from the trench and inside the Ninth Street Command tape, so there was no visual check.
The manager earlier said 6 of his 14 employees went back inside to shut down the presses. This recorder has not confirmed whether any are still inside.
It is on the trailer 2 clipboard with one entry: 'seepage, south wall, 16+00.' It is signed and has not been changed or added to.
Under fire department control. There is water in the trench and the box has not moved since 10:20 according to Rescue 2.

actionsTaken: 11:20: Wrote down the print shop manager's statement word for word
11:21: Wrote down the pipe crew laborer's statement word for word. The laborer's name is on the sign-in board.
11:22: Told the competent person and the Safety Director that both statements are recorded on this report
11:23: Left the LC-F-22 clipboard in trailer 2 as found. It has not been touched, copied or photographed.
recommendations: Engineer of Record to respond to the manager's statement about the existing crack and the CG-3 trend
Safety Director to decide how form LC-F-22 and the CG-3 logger data are held from now on
Superintendent to decide who answers the print shop manager and the 1 p.m. job request through Ninth Street Command
fields.photosNote: No photos taken. Scene is under Ninth Street Command control.
fields.marking: EXERCISE · EXERCISE · EXERCISE — NOT A SAFETY EVALUATION OF ANY REAL STRUCTURE

instructorNote: This is a red herring about re-entry and cause. Listen for three things: the EOR should explain that CG-3 measures movement since the 09:45 baseline, so the old crack does not explain the trend, and that re-entry is up to the building official. The competent person should refuse to change or add to LC-F-22. The Safety Director should secure the form and the CG-3 data as they are under LC-EAP-01 section 9, and nobody should state a cause.
